mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100k indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% occurs but SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200k and retail sales (RSAFS) below 500k signal collapsing consumer demand that triggers corporate revenue warnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1200 and RSAFS < 500k but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing slowdowns (INDPRO < 105), declining industrial production signals reduced corporate output capacity that lowers earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 105 but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200k, it indicates residential sector weakness that reduces household wealth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1200 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales index (RSAFS) above 510k indicates strong consumer spending that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 510k but SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and federal funds rate hikes (FEDFUNDS > 2.2%) signal accelerating inflation and tightening policy that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2.2% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS growth < 0) signals labor market fragility that reduces consumer confidence and corporate hiring, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth < 0 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
